## CELL FACTS

Cell 火_正财 (Fire carrying The Steward). Persona The Steward (正财). Definition line: "Methodical, directed acquisition, the value built and kept". Keyword Caution, charge gentle, poles catalyst Security / friction Hoarding. Family function: Action. Cost dimension: value built and kept; counting what others spend freely. Arena: granary, kept things, stone by stone, seasons of saving. Classical portrait: methodical, directed acquisition; value built and kept; caution, thrift, the slow ledger. Ruled domains: Wealth, Savings, Steady love. Sibling (other polarity of the family): 偏财.
Element arena: Fire (flame, light, warmth, fuel, the hearth, the blaze). dm_element (which core reads this cell): Water. structural_interaction seed: "Water directing Fire cross-polarity — depth shaping illumination into structured purpose".
- k2_overview: "Your Fire moves as the Steward: a hearth, not a bonfire. You keep warmth the way households keep flame, fed regularly, banked at night, never wasted on show. Your providing glows: steady income, warm table, festivals on schedule. It is the rarest fire, the kind that lasts."
- k2_functional: "You work in sustainable heat: consistent output that never needs rescue."
- adj_chips: {"catalyst":["Warm-handed","Hardworking","Bankable"],"friction":"[REDACTED: the words under test]"}
- k2_domain_readings: {"Wealth":"Your wealth is hearth-warm: earned brightly, spent on the household’s glow, kept steady over spectacular. Fund the gatherings and the securities both. A warm home is your portfolio’s purpose.","Savings":"You save for warmth: reserves that keep winters kind. Automate them so celebration cannot raid the woodpile. A banked fire relights fast. An empty grate does not.","Steady love":"You love like kept flame: daily warmth, faithful attention, romance on the calendar and off it. Your constancy is the gift. Add sparks deliberately so the hearth never assumes."}

- Sibling cell 火_偏财 friction row 0 drive passage, for the sibling test on the tension (this row must name a different either-or): "Every new shine gets your full sprint. The trend, the token, the just-opened thing: you arrive first, burn bright, and are gone before the substance question comes up. Chasing light is genuinely fun. A portfolio of chases, though, is mostly a photo album of exits."

Core element Water, energy element Fire. Law: Water tames Fire (水克火: rain ends the blaze). Relative to the core the energy is the tamed, so Fire is this core's Action. No chart is attached to this batch: the cell is written for every chart with a Water core that shows Fire on the friction pole, so no percentage and no state of one chart appears in any value. The friction pole of Fire as the Action is the Underfueled band's case (the core burns more than it takes in); tone by pole: reminder. Rows: row 0, row 1, row 2, each with its three angles (drive, cost_self, cost_others: the drive, the cost to the reader, the cost to others; the app shows one angle per row by position rotation, so each passage must stand alone); one chip per row, written once and copied byte-identical onto the row's three fields. value.text: You count everything, the money and the favours and the hours. Counting is your way of feeling safe, so knowing the total comes ahead of enjoying the thing. You keep yourself safe from loss and miss most of the pleasure along with it.

value_b.text: Nothing comes into your life without being counted first. Knowing the number settles you, and you check the balance more than you touch what it buys. You feel safe once the count is done, and you feel rich only when you spend some of it.

value.text: Playing it safe is your first answer. You would rather keep a small sure thing than try for a big maybe, because being safe is what lets you rest. Every time you play it safe, you are also picking which chance to miss.

value_b.text: Safe is the choice you make without noticing. Being covered feels better than being lucky to you, so you take the small sure return over the bigger maybe every time. Remember that each safe choice is paid for in the chances you let pass.

value.text: What you already have feels too precious to risk. Reaching for more feels like gambling, and you take the sure thing instead of the bigger one. Over the years, you give up more in missed chances than playing it safe ever saves you.

value.text: Without deciding to, you hold back warmth and money. Giving the whole of yourself feels like spending the last of something, and you give a careful portion rather than the full amount. You hold back more than you need to feel safe.

value_b.text: You keep part of everything back, warmth included. Running out is the fear underneath, and you would rather give a little less than find out what the full amount costs. Worth remembering that the warmth you hold back never reaches anyone, you included.

value.text: Keeping yourself back spares you hurt and costs you being known. You would rather hold back part of yourself than give the whole, so you stay half known. Remember that the closeness itself is what you lose, since what you keep back cannot be held.
